question: What has been done on applying LLMs to software engineering tasks, and what open problems remain?
hypothesis: Hybrid techniques (traditional SE plus LLMs) are the route to reliable LLM-based SE, since software execution gives automatable ground truth against which hallucinated output can be filtered.
contributions: Survey of LLM-based SE across requirements, code generation, testing, maintenance, documentation, analytics, HCI, process and education

limits: Authors say no survey of such a fast-moving area can be comprehensive; they give a snapshot as of mid-2023 (arXiv data to 27 July 2023, leaderboard 24 Aug 2023).
Almost all numbers are reported from other work and are not re-run; model rankings (HumanEval, SWE-bench) have dated.
arXiv keyword queries are approximate; authors draw only trend conclusions.
Table II lists WizardCoder and StarCoder as Encoder-only, which is likely a labelling error in the survey.
practices: Report model parameter settings such as temperature conspicuously to support replication (Sec XII-B).
Use execution and automated tests as ground truth to filter hallucinated code (Sec IV-E, XII-F).
Use the existing version as an 'Automated Regression Oracle' for refactoring and performance work, accepting that it bakes in current behaviour (Sec I).
Handle non-determinism with inferential statistics from SBSE, run repeatedly (Sec XII-E).
Evaluate code with strengthened test suites, since weak tests give false positives (Sec IV-D6).
Combine LLMs with search, test generation, static analysis or rankers rather than using them alone (Sec IV-C, XII-C).
